questions.scenario: Your school is hosting a massive talent show. What kind of magic act do you want to do?

options.text: A grand act with smoke, dramatic music, and making a whole teacher disappear.
Walking through the audience, doing mind-blowing card tricks right under their noses.
Having the principal think of a random word, and then revealing I had it written in an envelope all along.
I don't want to be on stage; I want to build the secret trapdoors and rigged boxes for the performer.

questions.scenario: How do you prefer to practice a new skill?

options.text: Practicing my dramatic timing, facial expressions, and poses in front of a full-length mirror.
Repeating a tiny, complex finger movement 1,000 times while watching TV until it's perfectly invisible.
Reading books on body language, psychology, and testing out word-play on my friends.
Sketching diagrams, measuring angles, and building cardboard prototypes of secret mechanisms.

questions.scenario: What type of puzzles do you naturally enjoy the most?

options.text: Escape rooms where there is a lot of theatrical lighting and a big, dramatic final exit.
Rubik's cubes, pen spinning, or anything that requires fast hand-eye coordination.
Riddles, logic paradoxes, and psychological games like 'Two Truths and a Lie'.
3D wooden or metal mechanical puzzles where I have to figure out hidden gears and locks.

questions.scenario: You make a mistake during a performance. How do you handle it?

options.text: I use a loud music cue or a flash of light to distract the audience while I fix it.
I use pure sleight of hand to smoothly switch to a different trick without anyone noticing the error.
I reframe the mistake and use psychology to make the audience think it was all part of the plan.
I immediately take apart the broken prop backstage and re-engineer the jammed mechanism so it never fails again.

questions.scenario: What fascinates you the most about the art of magic?

options.text: The spectacle—creating a sense of massive awe, wonder, and impossible scale.
The pure physical skill and dexterity required to manipulate objects invisibly.
Human behavior—how easily the brain and eyes can be hacked and fooled.
The secret engineering—how mirrors, magnets, and hidden wires can defy physics.

questions.scenario: Which movie or TV show style appeals to you the most?

options.text: The Greatest Showman or The Prestige—grand theater, costumes, and showmanship.
Now You See Me—fast-paced street magic, card throwing, and quick hands.
Sherlock or The Mentalist—hyper-observation, deduction, and reading people's deep secrets.
Iron Man or Hugo—tinkering in a workshop, inventing gadgets, and building complex machines.

questions.scenario: You and your friends are planning a harmless prank. What is your role?

options.text: The distraction—I put on a big, loud performance in the hallway so everyone looks at me.
The sneak—I am the one who silently slips the fake spider onto the desk without being seen.
The manipulator—I subtly convince the target to walk into the exact room we want them to.
The engineer—I rig the bucket of water and string so it drops at the absolute perfect moment.

questions.scenario: If you could instantly have one real superpower, what would it be?

options.text: Teleportation or Levitation—the ability to do physically impossible, grand things.
Super speed and agility in my hands—moving so fast it looks like time stopped.
Telepathy—the ability to hear what people are thinking and know their secrets.
Technopathy—the ability to look at any machine or object and instantly know how to rebuild it.

questions.scenario: How is your bedroom or workspace usually set up?

options.text: Decorated with cool posters, good lighting, and maybe a mirror for practicing my stage presence.
Scattered with decks of cards, coins, rubber bands, and small objects I constantly play with.
Filled with books on psychology, history, and human behavior.
A total mess of tools, glue, woodwork, wires, and half-built projects.

questions.scenario: What is the best possible reaction you could get from an audience?

options.text: A massive, roaring standing ovation from thousands of people in a huge theater.
Utter, speechless shock from a person standing just two feet away from me.
Someone looking genuinely spooked because they feel like I just 'read their soul'.
A famous magician telling me, 'I have absolutely no idea how you built that prop, it's genius.'

Stage_Illusionist.title: Stage Illusionist
Stage_Illusionist.primary_match_text: You are a natural showman. You love the spotlight, dramatic storytelling, and creating large-scale spectacles that leave massive crowds in awe.
Stage_Illusionist.day_in_the_life: Rehearsing choreography with assistants, designing dramatic lighting cues, and performing grand illusions like levitation or teleportation in large theaters or Vegas-style shows.
Stage_Illusionist.alternative_match_text: Because you love grand spectacles and commanding a stage, a career in Theater Acting, Event Directing, or Live Show Production is an excellent parallel path.
Stage_Illusionist.roadmap: Focus on Theater, Drama, and Public Speaking in high school. Join local magic clubs, study stage lighting/sound, and practice acting and dance to perfect your stage movement.

Close_up_Magician.title: Close-up / Sleight of Hand Artist
Close_up_Magician.primary_match_text: You are highly disciplined, detail-oriented, and love intimate interactions. You rely on pure physical skill and dexterity to create miracles right in front of people's eyes.
Close_up_Magician.day_in_the_life: Practicing complex card shuffles for hours, performing table-hopping magic at high-end corporate events, and creating viral street magic videos.
Close_up_Magician.alternative_match_text: Since you have incredible manual dexterity and patience, fields that require fine motor skills, like Playing an Instrument, Micro-surgery, or Precision Crafting, are strong backups.
Close_up_Magician.roadmap: Self-study through books like 'Royal Road to Card Magic'. Practice obsessively, perform for strangers to build confidence, and study basic psychology to master misdirection.

Mentalist.title: Mentalist / Mind Reader
Mentalist.primary_match_text: You are deeply analytical, observant, and fascinated by the human mind. You use psychology, suggestion, and body language to create the illusion of a sixth sense.
Mentalist.day_in_the_life: Memorizing massive amounts of information, predicting audience choices using psychological forces, and reading micro-expressions to guess what people are thinking.
Mentalist.alternative_match_text: Because you are a master of observation and human behavior, pursuing a degree in Psychology, Behavioral Analysis, or becoming a Detective/Interrogator is a perfect alternative.
Mentalist.roadmap: Take Psychology and Sociology in 11th/12th. Read extensively about body language, NLP (Neuro-Linguistic Programming), and memory techniques.

Illusion_Designer.title: Magic Inventor / Illusion Designer
Illusion_Designer.primary_match_text: You are a behind-the-scenes genius. You love solving complex problems, engineering hidden mechanics, and using physics and optics to make the impossible real.
Illusion_Designer.day_in_the_life: Using 3D software to design hidden compartments, building trapdoors in a woodworking shop, and selling exclusive, patented illusion designs to famous stage magicians.
Illusion_Designer.alternative_match_text: With your structural mindset and love for hidden mechanics, Mechanical Engineering, Special Effects (VFX/SFX) Design, or Theatrical Set Design are highly lucrative alternatives.
Illusion_Designer.roadmap: Take Science (PCM) in 11th/12th. Pursue Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Design, or Theatrical Tech. Learn CAD software, woodworking, and basic electronics.
